who: Judith E. Smith, historian of American social, urban and cultural history; Boston College 1981–1993, then UMass Boston; PhD Brown 1980.

evidence.says: Her own biography places her in Boston College history from 1981 to 1993, teaching urban, cultural and film history; it gives a PhD in American Civilization at Brown in 1980.

The authority identifies Judith E. Smith, author of Family Connections and Becoming Belafonte, as a UMass Boston American Studies professor and records her Brown PhD thesis, Remaking Their Lives (1980).

notes: Match inferred from the Boston College appointment and matching American urban/social history field. The supplied UC San Diego 1983 own_phd conflicts with both sources and appears misassociated; do not transfer it. The listed student relationships were not independently confirmed.

who: Richard Lee Turits, historian of Latin America and the Caribbean; formerly University of Michigan, later William & Mary; PhD Chicago 1997.

evidence.says: The authority records Richard Lee Turits as author of The Foundations of Despotism, a University of Chicago PhD thesis (1997).
His faculty biography gives a Chicago PhD and previous teaching in Michigan history, where he directed Latin American and Caribbean Studies in 2007–2012.
Michigan names Richard Turits as Graham Nessler’s dissertation advisor and as co-advisor of Edgardo Perez-Morales’s Itineraries of Freedom.

notes: Authority, doctorate and named Michigan students agree.

who: Thomas Wien, historian of New France and the Atlantic world at Université de Montréal; PhD history, McGill 1988.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Thomas Wien with the history department at Université de Montréal, citing Mémoires de Nouvelle-France (2005).
His institutional CV gives a McGill history PhD in 1988, Montréal faculty appointments from 1993 to 2022, and doctoral supervision of Didier, Dorais, Palomino and Ouellet.

notes: Exact doctorate and multiple listed doctoral students confirm the identity; some CV completion dates precede the AHA years.

who: Jeffrey S. Adler, historian of American urban life, crime and violence at the University of Florida; PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Jeffrey S. Adler, author of Murder in New Orleans, as a University of Florida professor of history and criminology.
Florida identifies Jeffrey S. Adler as its history professor specializing in urban history, violence and criminal justice, with a Harvard PhD.
The department’s alumni table names Jeffrey S. Adler as advisor of Alexander Tepperman and Adrienne Denoyelles, both PhDs in 2018, with the supplied dissertation titles.

notes: Authority and direct student links agree; the faculty biography confirms Harvard but does not specify the PhD year.

who: Michael D. Wise, history professor at the University of North Texas; PhD history, Minnesota 2012.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Michael D. Wise, author of Producing Predators (2016), as an assistant professor of history at the University of North Texas.
UNT’s faculty record names Michael D. Wise in History and gives a University of Minnesota history PhD in 2012.
Jared Ingram’s May 2020 UNT dissertation, Creeks and Open Spaces: Ned Fritz’s Environmental Crusades, lists Michael Wise as committee chair.

notes: Exact doctorate, institution and listed student identify Michael D. Wise.

who: Glennys Young, historian of Russia and the Soviet Union at the University of Washington; PhD Berkeley 1989.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Glennys Young, author of Power and the Sacred in Revolutionary Russia (1997), as a history and international studies professor at the University of Washington.
Washington gives her Berkeley PhD in 1989 and names her as chair of Amanda Swain’s 2013 and Andrew Stone’s 2012 dissertations, with the supplied titles.

notes: Exact doctorate and two named doctoral students confirm the match.

who: Laura A. Belmonte, historian of U.S. foreign relations at Oklahoma State University from 1996; PhD history, Virginia.

evidence.says: The authority links Laura A. Belmonte, editor of Speaking of America, to Oklahoma State’s history department as professor and head in 2016, specializing in U.S. foreign relations.
Oklahoma State’s 2018 profile says Belmonte joined in 1996 after completing her Virginia PhD; all her degrees were in history. She headed history from 2014 until June 2018.

notes: Authority affiliation in the students’ period and Virginia doctorate agree.

who: Edward Berenson, historian of modern France at New York University from 1998; PhD Rochester 1981.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Edward Berenson, author of Populist Religion and Left-Wing Politics in France and The Accusation, as an NYU history professor.
His own biography says he joined NYU in 1998 after teaching at UCLA and holds a Rochester PhD.
NYU’s 2019–2021 graduate bulletin lists Edward Berenson as professor of History and French Studies, PhD Rochester 1981, specializing in modern French social and cultural history.

notes: Authority, faculty chronology and exact doctorate agree with the supervisor record.
